task.title: fix: (?s).* prefix clipped to the suffix's line in ReverseSuffix/ReverseSuffixSet (regression in v0.12.15)
task.body:
With the `s` flag (`.` matches `\n`), patterns that start with `.*` and end in a literal suffix return a match that starts at the beginning of the suffix's line instead of the beginning of the input. This is a regression in v0.12.15; v0.12.14 returns the stdlib result for these patterns.

## Repro

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"regexp"

	"github.com/coregx/coregex"
)

func main() {
	for _, c := range [][2]string{
		{`(?s).*\.txt`, "a\nb.txt"},
		{`(?s).*\.(txt|log)`, "a\nb.log"},
		{`(?s).*\.txt`, "q.txt\nz\nb.txt"},
	} {
		std := regexp.MustCompile(c[0])
		cre := coregex.MustCompile(c[0])
		fmt.Printf("%-18q %-18q stdlib=%v coregex=%v\n", c[0], c[1],
			std.FindStringIndex(c[1]), cre.FindStringIndex(c[1]))
	}
}
```

v0.12.29:

```
"(?s).*\\.txt"     "a\nb.txt"         stdlib=[0 7] coregex=[2 7]
"(?s).*\\.(txt|log)" "a\nb.log"         stdlib=[0 7] coregex=[2 7]
"(?s).*\\.txt"     "q.txt\nz\nb.txt"  stdlib=[0 13] coregex=[8 13]
```

v0.12.14 prints the stdlib result for all three.

Wrong bounds also come from `FindAllStringIndex`, `FindStringSubmatchIndex` (including capture groups, e.g. `(?s)(.*)@example\.com` gives `[2 15 2 3]` instead of `[0 15 0 3]`), `ReplaceAllString` and `Split`. `MatchString` is correct.

Not affected: the same patterns without `(?s)` (they are correct, as fixed in #146), `(?s).+\.txt`, and `(?s).*\.txt$`.

Affected strategies: `UseReverseSuffix` (`(?s).*\.txt`, `(?s).*@example\.com`, `(?s).*(foo|bar)baz`, `(?s:.*)\.txt`) and `UseReverseSuffixSet` (`(?s).*\.(txt|log)`), checked with `COREGEX_DEBUG=1`.

## Cause

`hasDotStarPrefix` in `meta/strategy.go` returns true for both `OpStar(OpAnyChar)` (`(?s).*`) and `OpStar(OpAnyCharNotNL)` (`.*`). The result is passed as `matchStartZero` to `NewReverseSuffixSearcher` and `NewReverseSuffixSetSearcher` (`meta/compile.go`), and with that flag both searchers bound the match to the suffix's line via `lineStartBefore` and a line-end search, in `Find`, `FindAt` and `findIndicesAtImpl`. That line bound is right for `OpAnyCharNotNL` only. It came in with the `.*` newline-boundary fix in #146.

## Related: multiple suffixes across lines

`(?s).*\.txt` on `"q.txt\nz\nb.txt"` should be one greedy match `[0 13]`. Besides `Find` above (v0.12.15+), `FindAllStringIndex`, `FindStringSubmatchIndex`, `ReplaceAllString` and `Split` are wrong here already in v0.12.8, so this part predates #146:

| API | v0.12.8 | v0.12.29 |
|---|---|---|
| `FindStringIndex` | `[0 13]` ✓ | `[8 13]` |
| `FindAllStringIndex` | `[[0 5] [6 13]]` | `[[0 5] [8 13]]` |
| `FindStringSubmatchIndex` | `[0 5]` | `[0 5]` |
| `ReplaceAllString(s, "<>")` | `"<>\n<>"` | `"<>\nz\n<>"` | The fix for `(?s).*` should make all APIs agree on the greedy end.

## Expected behavior

For `(?s).*X`, the match starts at the search start and ends after the last `X` in the input, as in `regexp`.

## Context

Found in [uawk](https://github.com/kolkov/uawk), which prepends `(?s)` to every AWK regex (POSIX: `.` matches newline). With v0.12.29, `match("x\ny@example.com", /.*@example\.com/)` sets `RSTART=3` instead of 1, and `sub`/`split` with such patterns return wrong results on strings containing `\n`.

Refs #178
